newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Lockmaker Assa Abloy buys French Vachette.
newsitem.headline: Lockmaker Assa Abloy buys French Vachette.

text.p: Sweden's Assa Abloy, the world's largest lock maker, said on Wednesday it was buying French lock company Vachette for 1.1 billion francs ($189.5 million).
Assa Abloy said the purchase would be partly financed through a rights issue to shareholders that would raise 640 million crowns.
"Through the acquisition Assa Abloy would strengthen its position as the leading lock group in the world," Assa Abloy said in a statement.
"From 1998 onwards, the acquisition is expected to have a positive effect on earnings per share."

Assa Abloy said buying Vachette was a vital and logical step in its strategy to acquire market leading groups in Europe and the U.S. while growing organically in new, fast growing markets in Asia and Eastern Europe.

The Vachette group consists of cylinder and lock makers JPM, Laperche, Bezault, and Litto, the leading lock and cylinder company in Belgium. Vachette's annual sales for 1997 are expected to exceed 1.1 billion French francs.
The group is presently owned by Poliet in the Saint Gobain group, except for 50 percent of JPM that is owned by the Italian lock company Fincisa.
"After such an aquisition, Assa Abloy sales would amount pro forma to over 7.0 billion crowns," the company said.
Assa Abloy said the purchase would be partly financed through a rights issue and through an increase in Assa Abloy's existing multi-currency revolving credit.

The rights issue to existing shareholders would give one new share for 10 old shares at an issue price of 100 crowns. The issue was expected to be approved at the ordinary general sharesholder's meeting.
"Shareholders representing 43 percent of the share capital are positive to the rights issue and will subscribe for their parts," the company said.
The subscription period will run from May 26 to June 13.
Assa Abloy said the acquisition would take place after consultations with the employee representation committees and subject to necessary government approvals.
"Assa Abloy estimates that rationalisation and synergies will lead to considerable profit improvements for the group within a few years," the statement said.
"The business is well invested and is expected to generate a positive cash flow after acquisition costs already in 1997."
